LESSON: SONGS

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: PERFORMING
Topic 1.1: Songs

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Songs. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: When is the national types of songs performed anthem sung?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. sing 3-part rounds, keeping verses of the Kenya National Anthem in to the respective parts for English and or Kiswahili paying enjoyment attention to posture and appropriate

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SONGS
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Songs helps you succeed in MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: SONGS
Study Songs like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Sing 3-part rounds, keeping verses of the Kenya National Anthem in to the respective parts for English and or Kiswahili paying enjoyment attention to posture and appropriate

What this means
In this part you learn to sing 3-part rounds, keeping verses of the Kenya National Anthem in to the respective parts for English and or Kiswahili paying enjoyment attention to posture and appropriate. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: sing 3-part rounds, keeping verses of the Kenya National Anthem in to the respective parts for English and or Kiswahili paying enjoyment attention to posture and appropriate.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Songs” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can sing 3-part rounds, keeping verses of the Kenya National Anthem in to the respective parts for English and or Kiswahili paying enjoyment attention to posture and appropriate. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Songs is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Songs” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: sing 3-part rounds, keeping verses of the Kenya National Anthem in to the respective parts for English and or Kiswahili paying enjoyment attention to posture and appropriate)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Songs to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: sing 3-part rounds, keeping verses of the Kenya National Anthem in to the respective parts for English and or Kiswahili paying enjoyment attention to posture and appropriate.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Songs from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Songs: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Songs?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. When is the national types of songs performed anthem sung?
2. when singing b) sing a variety of age songs, action songs, sacred songs and the national anthem?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Songs means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: sing 3-part rounds, keeping verses of the Kenya National Anthem in to the respective parts for English and or Kiswahili paying enjoyment attention to posture and appropriate.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
